title: Sakya
hookLine: the school of the gray earth, led by the Khon family

lines: A SCHOOL NAMED FOR THE GROUND.
cards: A hillside in southern Tibet, and the soil on it is pale. Not brown, not red: a dusty, ashy gray, the color of a cooled fire.
Tradition says a man of the Khon family built a monastery on that slope, and the place took its name from the ground under it. Sakya. The gray earth.

A whole school of Tibetan Buddhism is named for a patch of dirt, and for a long time one family led it, parents and children and nephews, handing the work down at home as much as from the teaching throne.

teach.h: GRAY EARTH: A SCHOOL WITH AN ADDRESS.
teach.b: First, the name. Sakya is usually translated as gray earth, or pale earth, after that hillside. Plenty of schools carry a founder's name or an idea.
This one is named for a place you could kneel down and touch: in this school, the teaching has an address. Second, the family.

teach.h: THE KHON FAMILY HOLDS THE THRONE.
teach.b: The Sakya tradition remembers the Khon family as its holders.

teach.h: SAKYA PANDITA AND HIS NEPHEW PHAGPA.
teach.b: Leadership passed down within that family, often from uncle to nephew, and the head of the school came to be called the Sakya Trizin, the holder of the Sakya throne.
In some traditions authority moves by election or by finding a reborn teacher.

teach.h: A LINEAGE THAT IS ALSO A HOUSEHOLD.
teach.b: In this one, for much of its story, it moved through a household. Third, the scholar. Out of that family came Sakya Pandita, remembered as a great learned man.
He wrote on logic and on how to read the teachings carefully, and he wrote short verses of good advice about speaking, giving and choosing friends, short enough to remember.
His nephew Phagpa traveled to the court of the Mongol rulers, and tradition says he devised a written script for them.
A family from a gray hillside ended up teaching at the edge of an empire. Fourth, what a family carries. A lineage is usually pictured as a line of teachers.
Sakya adds something warmer and messier: kitchens, inheritances, a young person who grows up knowing the teaching is the family business and has to decide whether to take it on.
The teaching came down through ordinary people, who had to agree to carry it.

how: Sakya Buddhists study and practice in monasteries and centers of the Sakya school, honoring the Sakya Trizin as the head of the tradition and the Khon family as its historic holders.

games.why: the line came down through a household, but each holder still had to take it up. a lineage is people choosing to carry something.

practice: Bring to mind one family's story, your own, a friend's, or one you've only heard about, and one thing handed down in it: a recipe, a trade, a phrase, a way of praying, a stubbornness.
Ask quietly who first carried it, and who chose to keep carrying it. You don't need answers; let the question rest, the way the gray earth rests under the monastery.
